scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Skudrinka is a traditional Macedonian oro originating from the Dolna Reka region, located along the Radika River in western North Macedonia.
The dance forms part of the traditional village repertoire of the region's Macedonian population.

In 1977, ethnomusicologist Mihailo Dimovski formally documented the dance in his publication Macedonian Folk Dances (Македонски народни ора), issued in Skopje by Naša kniga and the Institut za folklor.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Skudrinka is a traditional community oro (folk dance).
In modern contexts, it is performed by Macedonian folk ensembles such as 'Orce Nikolov' as part of the country's national stage dance repertoire.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance begins with performers arranged in a half-circle formation.
Rather than holding hands directly, the dancers hold sticks placed between each participant, keeping their hands in a horizontal position.
The movement is characterized by steady steps performed on the half-feet, interspersed with turns and vertical jumps.
Watch for Stick hold position, Half-foot turn and jump.

Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Half-circle chain formation traveling along a curved path.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Skudrinka is danced to a 2/4 meter rhythm.

Specific traditional instruments for the Dolna Reka region are not detailed in the available primary source text, though performance groups execute the piece to traditional Macedonian folk arrangements.
Listen for the Traditional Macedonian folk instruments.
The pulse is 2/4 at about 105 beats a minute.
A steady, driving 2/4 Balkan folk rhythm designed to support synchronized half-foot steps, turns, and jumps in a line formation.
